gate.name: fusion_max_tess_to_vision_ratio
gate.rule: skip fusion LLM call when (vision_text non-empty) AND (tess_text non-empty) AND (len(tess_text) > 1.5 * len(vision_text))

holdout.reason: stress-test: model confuses Devanagari for Gujarati
holdout.note: Gate's silence preserved the real win. Without the gate, fusion would still have run (and won). With the gate firing incorrectly here, we would have lost the only winning strategy for this page.

holdout.reason: re-photo of p10 with a worse image; tests if the gate is stable across re-photos
holdout.winner: fusion on CER (92.3 < 139.9), vision on score (2 > 1); both are near the floor, gate silent, correct
holdout.note: Tesseract was too short to trigger the noise heuristic (ratio 0.08 << 1.5), so the gate's silence is the right call: nothing to skip. Reading the metrics honestly: fusion did marginally better on CER (92.3 vs vision's 139.9, lower is better), but vision's score was 1 point higher (2 vs 1). CER and score can disagree (model variance is real); the gate's correctness here is on the *ratio condition*, not on which path 'won' overall. p-11 is a hard page — both pages in the holdout are near-floor cases.

verdict.recommendation: Keep the gate. It does not help p03 or p11 (the gate's silence is the right call on both — tesseract is normal-length on p03, essentially empty on p11), and it cleanly avoids the documented p05/p07 regression where fusion hurt CER. The gate's only function is to skip when tesseract is suspiciously long; it is silent (correctly) when tesseract is normal-length or empty. CER and score can disagree, and reading either metric backwards is a real risk — this file was originally written that way on p-11 and has been corrected.
